name: Midheaven Psychology
description: Defines needs, sensitivities, defensive strategies, regulation needs, blind spots, and integration markers for public actualization.

coreNeed.definition: A workable way to bring capacities into visible social participation through roles, responsibilities, contribution, and public accountability.

coreMotivation.definition: Translate ability, effort, and purpose into forms that can function in the wider social world.

coreSensitivity.definition: Heightened awareness of being observed, evaluated, recognized, or overlooked.
Heightened awareness of whether a public role matches actual capacities and responsibilities.
Heightened awareness of whether visible activity creates value beyond the private sphere.
Heightened awareness of public expectations, legitimacy, accountability, and influence.

coreFearPatterns.definition: Fear that visible participation will expose incapacity, inconsistency, or unpreparedness.
Fear of being seen without making a real contribution.
Fear that a public role will become fixed and consume the wider identity.
Fear that contribution will remain unseen, unsupported, or socially irrelevant.

protectiveStrategies.definition: Use title, prestige, or external recognition as a substitute for actual contribution.
Reduce public participation to avoid evaluation or responsibility.
Treat the public role as the entire self.
Manage public expression so tightly that spontaneity, adaptation, or learning is reduced.
Assign legitimacy or responsibility entirely to external authority figures.

blindSpots: Confusing public role with total identity
Treating career as the only expression of actualization

regulationNeeds.definition: Keep public role distinct from total identity.
Identify the actual value, function, or service created by public participation.
Match exposure and responsibility to current capacity.
Maintain contact with private foundations, internal support, and restoration.
Use public response to refine role performance without converting feedback into identity judgment.

healthyPsychologicalFunctions: Assume responsibility without total role identification
Use recognition as feedback rather than proof of worth
Coordinate public participation with private foundations
Accept authority proportionate to actual responsibility
Revise roles as capacities and contexts change
Distinguish public impact from image management
integrationMarkers: Can be visible without performing status
Can contribute without overidentifying with role
Can revise public direction after feedback
Can withdraw for restoration without seeing it as failure
Can coordinate Midheaven and Imum Coeli reference frames
reflectionComponents: What capacity is being actualized here?
What contribution is this role making?
Is this visibility serving function or image?
How is the private foundation supporting public participation?
What would remain valuable without recognition?
psychologyConstraints: No career outcome may be guaranteed.
No status or fame claim may be inferred from the Midheaven alone.
Public role must remain distinct from total identity.
The Imum Coeli must remain available as the foundational opposite reference frame.
Developmental language must reference the global development blueprint.

provenance.sourcePolicy: Reference-frame vocabulary only. Psychology and development qualify public actualization but do not redefine the Midheaven as career, status, fame, or guaranteed achievement.
